familiar.bench.empty: The bench: for a token, a framed map or a gridded map that belongs to no one-shot. Add pictures with the button above and work on them here; they land under Oneshots\Bench, which Open the folder shows, and nothing here is written for a VTT.
familiar.caption: Caption or note
familiar.description: Maps gridded or gridless, tokens cut round with a ring, handouts framed, on their own or as a one-shot kit with its run sheet, written for Foundry or Roll20 the way each wants it.
familiar.empty: Nothing in this kit yet. Add pictures with the button above, choosing whether they are maps, tokens or handouts, or drop a folder of maps into the kit's maps folder and press Refresh.
familiar.encounter.name: Name
familiar.encounter.roster.hint: One line per group: 3 Goblin, Goblin x3, Goblin (3). A line matching a token by name is placed on the map; any other line travels as text.
familiar.encounter.roster.placeholder:
3 Goblin
Bugbear
the barkeep hides behind the counter
familiar.encounters.empty: The run sheet: one entry per fight, on which map, who is in it, and what to remember. Foundry gets a journal page per entry, linked from its scene, with the tokens placed hidden on the map.
familiar.error.benchname: Bench is the standing kit's name; pick another.
familiar.error.nameclash: There is already a {0} in that folder.
familiar.export.foundry.hint: A folder with every picture and a kit.json the meows-kit module reads: one scene per map, gridded or not, in this order, in a folder named after the kit.
familiar.export.roll20.hint: Roll20 has no way in, so this is the files spelled its way: maps sized to whole 70 px units so the grid lines up on upload, numbered in order, under the limit, and a ROLL20.md saying which page gets which.
familiar.fit.hint: Down to that longest side, as WebP, or PNG if it has transparency. The grid number scales with it. The original stays under originals.
familiar.frame.hint: A border outside the picture, never over it: the canvas grows and the grid stays where it was. Parchment, stone, wood, gilt and torn paper ship; your own go in the frames folder below.
familiar.frames.count: {0} rings, {1} backgrounds, {2} borders; {3} of them yours.
familiar.frames.hint: Drop your own PNGs in: token-*.png for a ring (transparent middle, the cut measured from it), background-*.png for a disc behind the picture, border-*.png for a 9-slice border. A name matching a shipped frame replaces it. Refresh reads them again.
familiar.grid.enabled.hint: Untick it for a map played without one. The VTT then gets a gridless scene and the size is in pixels, which is a choice rather than a missing number.
familiar.grid.none.long: Gridless. The scene is measured in pixels.
familiar.grid.squares.long: {0} × {1} squares, {2} px each. Check the blue lines sit on the map's own lines.
familiar.name: Name, as the VTT shows it
familiar.notes.empty: Markdown files under notes. Each one becomes a journal entry in Foundry, in this order. Make one with the box above.
familiar.notes.unsaved: Not saved yet; saved when you switch or press Save.
familiar.status.exported.foundry: {0} files written to {1}. Upload that folder through Foundry's file picker and press Import a kit in the meows-kit module.
familiar.status.exported.roll20: {0} files written to {1}. ROLL20.md in there says what to do with each.
familiar.status.fitted: {0} fitted: {1} to {2}. The original is under originals.
familiar.status.framed: {0} framed with {1}, {2} px added on every side; the grid did not move.
familiar.status.start: Pick a kit on the left, or make one.
familiar.status.token: {0} cut round with {1}. The original is under originals.
familiar.title: Familiar
familiar.token.hint: A background disc if one is chosen, the picture inside the ring, the ring on top, and nothing outside the ring. 512 × 512 PNG, which is what a VTT wants a token to be. The original stays under originals.
